cards.title: Doctor's handwriting, decoded a little
cards.body: Prescriptions use Latin shorthand that has been around for ages. Knowing a few common ones helps you ask better questions.

cards.title: OD: once a day
cards.body: One dose in a day. The prescription or the doctor should say when, like morning or night.

cards.title: BD: twice a day
cards.body: Two doses a day, usually morning and night. On many Indian prescriptions you'll see the same thing written as 1-0-1.

cards.title: TDS: three times a day
cards.body: Three doses spread across the day, like morning, afternoon and night. You may also see it as 1-1-1.

cards.title: HS: at bedtime
cards.body: Take it at night, before sleeping. If you're unsure whether that's different from "after dinner" for this medicine, ask.

cards.title: SOS: only if needed
cards.body: Not a regular dose. Take it only when the symptom shows up, within the limit the doctor gives. Ask what that limit is.

cards.title: Not sure? Ask, don't guess
cards.body: Shorthand varies between doctors, and handwriting can mislead. If anything is unclear, check with the doctor or pharmacist before the first dose.

takeaway: OD is once, BD twice, TDS three times, HS at bedtime and SOS only when needed. Confirm anything unclear with your pharmacist.
